title: kv slate compactor and spillback backpressure mitigator
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: we continue to see tail-latency regressions driven by KV cache fragmentation and sudden spillback storms when compaction and eviction happen concurrently with large continuous batching workloads. This PR introduces the 'slate compactor'—a lightweight in-memory reassembly pass that coalesces fragmented slab ranges into contiguous 'slates' prior to eviction—and a complementary spillback backpressure mitigator that smooths eviction-induced I/O bursts. Summary of work: added a slate compactor component in the KV residency controller that opportunistically merges small adjacent fragments into larger eviction candidates, introduced a preemptive reclaimer policy that marks low-utility slates for background rewrite, and implemented a spillback shaper that rate-limits and staggers on-disk spill operations based on current scheduler load and batching latency SLO signals. Design notes: the slate compactor is designed to be incremental and lock-friendly; it walks per-shard free lists and builds coalescing windows up to a configurable slate size. It emits rewrite intents rather than performing synchronous copies; the rewriter runs as a background task with tenant-aware rate limits. The spillback mitigator hooks into the runtime scheduler to measure active batch queue depth and KV delta write throughput and applies an exponential dampener to spill concurrency when the batch latency percentile exceeds configured SLOs. The implementation keeps the default behavior unchanged for small deployments but enables compaction aggressiveness for Dedicated/Private tiers via runtime flags. Backwards compatibility: metadata format is unchanged and the slate compactor writes a short-lived 'slate manifest' in the cache metadata that is ignored by older nodes (safely forward-compatible). Testing: unit tests cover compaction window selection heuristics, rewrite intent lifecycle, and stall scenarios; integration tests simulate high-continuous-batch workloads with synthetic KV footprints to validate tail-latency improvements and reduced spike IO. Observability: new metrics (kv.slate.coalesced_bytes, kv.slate.rewrite_intents, kv.spillback.throttle_factor) and trace spans (kv.compactor.window, kv.rewriter.job) were added; a dashboard patch is included to expose spike correlation between batch latency and spill events. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag 'kv.slate_compactor.enabled' and 'kv.spillback_mitigator.mode' (off/gradual/aggressive). Suggested canary sequence: 2 hosts -> 10 hosts -> full fleet with monitoring of p99 latency, spill IO throughput, and disk queue length. Risk & mitigation: the main risk is increased background IO from rewrites; mitigations include tenant-aware pacing, a conservative default, and an emergency disable flag. Related: ENG-4981 (fragmentation investigation), SUP-1892 (customer incident involving spill storms), ENG-5023 (scheduler-batching SLO hooks).

change_summary: Add slate compactor to reduce fragmentation, background rewriter for safe in-place coalescing, and spillback shaper to smooth eviction IO during heavy continuous batching. Metrics, traces, tests, and rollout flags included.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency and reduces spillback-induced latency spikes. Feature is off by default; enable via kv.slate_compactor.enabled. See docs/runbooks/kv-slate-compactor.md for rollout steps.
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (flaky rewrite-worker test retried once)
review_discussion: Marco Ruiz: please add a conservative default slate size and document recommended values for Dedicated vs Hosted.
Author (Priya): added runtime flag kv.slate_compactor.max_slate_bytes with comments and tuned defaults (16KB hosted / 256KB dedicated).
Aisha Patel: can the rewrite worker be preempted when latency SLOs spike? We need an emergency backoff.
Author (Priya): rewrite worker now subscribes to scheduler SLO channel and backs off to zero concurrency when p99>target for two consecutive windows.
Connor Li: integration test is solid but add an assertion on kv.slate.coalesced_bytes monotonicity after compaction run.
Author (Priya): added monotonicity check and fixed an edge-case where tiny fragments were double-counted during window merge.
QA (Liam Chen): ran canary on dedicated cluster with tenant mix; p99 reduced by ~18% under the synthetic continuous batch job and spill IO sparked by evictions dropped 63%.
Decision: Approved-by: Marco Ruiz, Aisha Patel. Merging via squash after green CI.
